summary: The task was an oncology follow-up panel harmonization that failed verification. The agent made a critical error by rounding values to 2 decimal places, which violated the clinical-lab-harmonization skill's explicit rule: 'DO NOT ROUND. The verifier expects full-precision floats (tolerance ~1e-4). Any rounding causes failure.' The agent also deviated from the established skill by using different conversion thresholds and factors not documented in the reference tables. Additionally, the agent incorrectly applied conversion logic for certain analytes (e.g., using albumin threshold of ≥10 instead of >60 g/L). The existing clinical-lab-harmonization skill covers this capability well but needs expansion to explicitly include oncology panels and reinforce the no-rounding rule with specific examples of the failure mode seen here.
